R701.note: Allowlist correctly closes dynamic-include injection, but the placeholder plugin names ('summary','details','preview') are guessed and any real plugin not in the list silently falls back to 'summary' instead of erroring - write-up discloses this ('update with actual plugin names').

R702.note: CrossOriginProtection + DELETE correctly closes CSRF, but the source comments state the endpoint was deliberately GET so an email link could trigger it directly - switching to DELETE silently breaks that click-to-delete flow with no disclosure or mention.

R703.note: Path.resolve()+is_relative_to() correctly closes both the symlink-follow and string-prefix bypasses; behavior otherwise unchanged.

R704.note: Verified: still wraps in sh -c/cmd.exe /c, so splitting into argList.add("echo"); argList.add(param) makes param become the shell's $0, not an argument to echo (confirmed by running sh -c echo X, which prints nothing) - injection is closed but the echoed response silently goes empty, and the write-up's explanation of the mechanism is wrong.

R705.note: Verified: ObjectInputFilter.Config.setSerialFilter() throws IllegalStateException if called more than once (reproduced), but onMessage() calls it on every JMS message, so the listener throws on every message after the first; should use ois.setObjectInputFilter(filter) per-stream instead of the static VM-wide setter.

R706.note: CBC+random IV (or GCM alt) correctly replaces ECB; IV-prepending format change is inherent to the fix and explicitly described.

R707.note: Correctly validates bytesRead before the signature comparison, matching the exact reported sink; no other behavior change.

R708.note: Moves uid into the parameterized Object[] array with correct {0}/{1} index mapping; search semantics unchanged.

R709.note: Standard sqlx parameterized query; matches original query/columns exactly.

R710.note: Narrows CSRF exemption to /api/webhooks/** exactly as the case's own comments specify; no other change.

R711.note: Adds the missing ownership check (in-handler and DB-scoped options); consistent 404-for-both-cases handling avoids an enumeration oracle.

R712.note: Replaces GroovyShell with a deny-by-default JEXL sandbox plus a character allowlist; sample formula from the source docstring still evaluates correctly, and the try/catch fallback to basePrice is disclosed.

R713.note: Adds a bounds check against record.size() before the indexed write, matching the case exactly; skip-vs-throw tradeoff explicitly discussed.

R714.note: Restores signature verification with an explicit algorithms allowlist; placeholder secret is clearly marked and followed by guidance to store it securely.

R715.note: proc_open array form correctly bypasses the shell; matches case's grep/logPath usage exactly.

R716.note: Whitelisted orderBy() replaces orderByRaw(); default sort value 'created_at desc' from the controller is itself on the allowlist, so legitimate default use still works; exception-on-reject behavior is disclosed.

R717.note: Allowlist regex (with an RFC 4515 escaping alternative) correctly closes LDAP filter injection; rest of the flow unchanged.

R718.note: strlcat is not part of standard C or traditional glibc (only glibc >=2.38, BSD, or macOS provide it without extra includes/libbsd), so this risks a real compile/link failure on many common toolchains; a portable snprintf-based bound check would avoid that risk. Behavior for the case in question is otherwise correct and matches the existing out_size check.

R719.note: SQLAlchemy bound parameter replaces f-string interpolation; identical query semantics.

R720.note: Standard PreparedStatement with '?' placeholder; correctly notes the finally-block statement variable must also be updated.

R721.note: RFC 2254-style hex escaping of LDAP metacharacters closes the injection; filter structure otherwise unchanged.

R722.note: Trailing-separator-aware prefix check (with filepath.Rel alternative) correctly excludes the uploads-backup sibling-directory bypass; matches the case exactly.

R723.note: Classic pre-multiplication overflow check (size > MAX_VALUE/count) correctly prevents the wraparound; same reject path/status as the existing bounds check.

R724.note: DatabaseFacade.ExecuteSqlAsync(FormattableString) is a real EF Core API (confirmed) that auto-parameterizes interpolated values; all three values now bound, same update semantics.

R725.note: Corrects the off-by-one loop bound (i <= n to i < n); matches the function's documented n = min(history_len, max_out) contract exactly.

R726.note: Verified against RestrictedPython 8.5: compile_restricted() returns a plain code object with no .errors or .code attribute, so 'if byte_code.errors' raises AttributeError on every single invocation - the primary fix crashes before exec ever runs, breaking the endpoint entirely and silently (not disclosed); the fallback minimal-builtins option is not the fix given as primary.

R727.note: Correctly tracks the record offset instead of the raw pointer and recomputes last_write_ptr from the post-realloc base; matches the case's struct fields and return type exactly.

R728.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection and adds the hook to the route, matching the file's own missing-registration comment; client-side token requirement is disclosed.

R729.note: Django .raw() with %s placeholder and parameter list correctly replaces f-string interpolation; same query.

R730.note: std::min(dataLen, frame.payload.size()) correctly bounds the write using the real std::array-backed struct, but oversized input is now silently truncated with no error returned to the caller - disclosed in prose as an accepted tradeoff, not surfaced as an error to the caller.

R731.note: Adds secure=True (plus SameSite as defense-in-depth) to the exact set_cookie call; no other behavior change.

R732.note: Column allowlist correctly prevents ORDER BY injection, but the controller's own default sort value ('created_at', used whenever ?sort= is omitted) is not in the {Id,Name,Status} allowlist, so the default/most common call to this endpoint now throws an exception - not disclosed or checked against the actual call chain.

R733.note: Files.newDirectoryStream eliminates the shell entirely, closing the injection, but the added validation rejects any input containing '/' or '\\' and then silently returns with no response body/status set - since the original command took data as an ls-style path argument, this silently breaks the realistic (path-containing) legitimate use case with an empty 200 response, undisclosed.

R734.note: StackExchange.Redis StringSet() correctly closes RESP command injection via length-prefixed arguments, but requires swapping the controller's DI dependency from Socket to IConnectionMultiplexer; write-up states this is required but doesn't show the (needed) DI registration update.

R735.note: Pre-validation plus normpath + relative_to confinement check correctly closes both absolute-path and traversal-sequence bypasses; matches the case exactly.

R736.note: Verified against gorilla/sessions source: CookieStore.New() still decodes any existing request cookie and sets IsNew=false exactly like Get() when a cookie is present, so an attacker-planted session cookie is not discarded - the write-up's core claim ('fresh session with an empty ID') is false for this store type, and the case file's own comment already flags that gorilla/sessions has no built-in ID rotation. The added Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite hardening is harmless but doesn't compensate.

R737.note: AesGcm with a fresh random 12-byte nonce and stored tag correctly replaces ECB; nonce+tag storage format change is explicit and necessary for decryption.

R738.note: Verified: csrf-csrf's doubleCsrf() defaults ignoredMethods to [GET,HEAD,OPTIONS], and the case's doubleCsrf() call doesn't override it, so adding doubleCsrfProtection to a GET route (the primary fix given) is a no-op - the middleware skips validation on GET entirely, leaving the route exactly as exploitable as before. The stated 'alternative' (move to DELETE) would work but isn't the fix given and isn't fully specified (email-link change not shown).

R739.note: Extension map is derived from the verified detectedType instead of the client-supplied filename, and matches the case's own allowedContentTypes set exactly.

R740.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check with rooted-path rejection correctly closes traversal; matches the case's _basePath exactly.
